name: Question 8
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=3-3{t}^{2},$ where $t⩾0$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=2\,\text{s},$ calculate the maximum velocity ${v}_{\text{max}}$ of the particle and determine the time whan the particle reaches its maximum velocity.
worked_solution:
The extrema of the velocity $v$ occur at the critical points of $v.$

Since $\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}=a(t),$ to find the times where $v$ is a maximum, we just need to solve $a(t)=0$ and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving $a(t)=0$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t) & =0 \\ 3-3{t}^{2} & =0 \\ 3(1-t)(1+t) & =0 \\ t & =\pm 1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $t⩾0$, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when $t=1\,\text{s}.$

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of $v(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=1:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}^{″}(t) & =\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}v}{\text{d}{t}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(a(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3-3{t}^{2}) \\  & =-6t \\ {v}^{″}(1) & =-6(1) \\  & =-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${v}^{″}(1)<0,$ we conclude that the velocity is maximized when $t=1\,\text{s}.$

Now, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3-3{t}^{2})\text{d}t \\  & =3t-{t}^{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $v(2)=2.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}3(2)-{2}^{3}+C & =2 \\ 6-8+C & =2\,⟹\,C=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the velocity $v$ of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=4+3t-{t}^{3}.$

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

$$
{v}_{\text{max}}=v(1)=4+3(1)-{1}^{3}=6\,\text{m}/\text{s}
$$

Question 8
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=3−3t2, where t⩾0 is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=2s, calculate the maximum velocity vmax of the particle and determine the time whan the particle reaches its maximum velocity.

a
vmax=6m/s,t=1s
b
vmax=4m/s,t=0s
c
vmax=15m/s,t=2s
d
vmax=3m/s,t=0s
e
vmax=8m/s,t=1s
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The extrema of the velocity v occur at the critical points of v.

Since dvdt=a(t), to find the times where v is a maximum, we just need to solve a(t)=0 and test each solution using the first or second derivative test.

Solving a(t)=0 gives a(t)=03−3t2=03(1−t)(1+t)=0t=±1.

Since t⩾0, the extremum of the velocity function occurs when t=1s.

We now test the extreme value using the second derivative test. For this, we find the second derivative of v(t) and evaluate it at t=1:

v″(t)=d2vdt2=ddt(dvdt)=ddt(a(t))=ddt(3−3t2)=−6tv″(1)=−6(1)=−6.

Since v″(1)<0, we conclude that the velocity is maximized when t=1s.

Now, we find v(t) by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

v(t)=∫a(t)dt=∫(3−3t2)dt=3t−t3+C To determine C, we use the fact that v(2)=2. Substituting this into the above gives 3(2)−23+C=26−8+C=2⟹C=4.

Therefore, the velocity v of the particle at time t is v(t)=4+3t−t3.

Finally, we calculate the maximum velocity:

vmax=v(1)=4+3(1)−13=6m/s
